# Unit test for function circular_shift
def test_circular_shift():
    # Basic circular shift: shift last digit to front
    assert circular_shift(12, 1) == "21"
    assert circular_shift(12345, 2) == "45123"
    assert circular_shift(12345, 1) == "51234"

    # Shift equal to length returns original string
    assert circular_shift(12, 2) == "12"
    assert circular_shift(100, 3) == "100"
    assert circular_shift(0, 1) == "0"

    # Shift greater than length returns reversed string
    assert circular_shift(12, 3) == "21"
    assert circular_shift(100, 4) == "001"
    assert circular_shift(97, 8) == "79"

    # Zero shift returns original string
    assert circular_shift(1234, 0) == "1234"

    # Negative integer input
    assert circular_shift(-12, 1) == "2-1"

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_circular_shift()

def test_circular_shift():
    # Basic circular shifts (shift right by given positions)
    assert circular_shift(12, 1) == "21"
    assert circular_shift(12, 2) == "12"
    assert circular_shift(1234, 1) == "4123"
    assert circular_shift(1234, 2) == "3412"
    assert circular_shift(1234, 3) == "2341"
    assert circular_shift(1234, 4) == "1234"

    # Shift greater than number of digits -> reversed string
    assert circular_shift(12, 3) == "21"
    assert circular_shift(1234, 5) == "4321"
    assert circular_shift(100, 4) == "001"

    # Edge cases
    assert circular_shift(0, 1) == "0"       # shift == len(s), full rotation
    assert circular_shift(0, 2) == "0"       # shift > len(s), reversed
    assert circular_shift(7, 0) == "7"       # zero shift
    assert circular_shift(10, 1) == "01"     # leading zero after shift
    assert circular_shift(1000000, 2) == "001000"  # leading zeros preserved
